Investors wipe $2.5T off Nasdaq as blue tsunami prompts AI fears reuters.com · 32 points · 9 comments · HN thread The article could not be read, so this summary is based on the title and the discussion. TL;DR A Reuters report says Nasdaq lost about $2.5 trillion in value after the 2026 midterm elections produced a Democratic sweep, with AI and data center stocks sliding on concerns about expansion plans. The article could not be read, so this summary rests on the headline, URL and comments. Headline says investors wiped $2.5 trillion off the Nasdaq after a 'blue tsunami' election result. Reported selloff is attributed to fears for AI and data center stocks and their expansion plans. The URL dates the story to November 5, 2026. Two related HN threads describe Nasdaq falling about 4% into correction territory. Discussion The thread is small and mostly argues about why data center and AI stocks might fall after a Democratic election sweep. One commenter says the drop is ordinary market dynamics with no conspiracy involved. Others treat the political angle as a shift in public sentiment against data centers, and a few mock the idea that Democrats are anti-tech. The mood is skeptical and somewhat combative, with more jabs than data. Market drop is normal rotation, not a political plot (some): One commenter argues that stocks often move inversely to good news and that a fall signals a change in market dynamics, not a conspiracy tied to who governs. Opposition is public sentiment against data centers (some): Commenters say voters across parties oppose local data centers over environmental and NIMBY concerns, so the Democratic label is incidental. Calling Democrats anti-tech is absurd (a few): Several replies mock the label with analogies, arguing that a stance on one issue does not make a party anti-tech or anti-life. Slowing AI through data center limits is short-sighted (a few): One commenter describes a Reddit thread where restricting data centers is framed as a way to slow AI, and argues research would not stop anyway. Sismo de magnitud 6.1 sacude Sinaloa; reportan epicentro cerca de Guasave Un sismo de magnitud 6.1 se registró al suroeste de Guasave, Sinaloa, con una profundidad de cinco kilómetros. El movimiento ocurrió el 30 de junio de 2026 y generó réplicas en la región. Por Gabriela Díaz | Reportera Un sismo de magnitud 6.1 se registró frente a las costas de Sinaloa, con epicentro localizado a 116 kilómetros al suroeste de Guasave, informó el Servicio Sismológico Nacional (SSN). El movimiento telúrico ocurrió el 30 de junio de 2026, a las 13:45:36 horas, tiempo del centro de México, con una profundidad de cinco kilómetros. El fenómeno fue reportado en una región del Golfo de California. Durante las horas posteriores se registraron movimientos adicionales, por lo que las autoridades mantuvieron el monitoreo de la actividad sísmica. SSN reporta réplicas después del sismo en Guasave El Servicio Sismológico Nacional informó que hasta las 15:00 horas del 30 de junio se habían registrado 10 réplicas del movimiento principal, cuya magnitud fue de 6.1. La réplica de mayor intensidad alcanzó una magnitud de 4.9, de acuerdo con los reportes difundidos por el organismo. Las réplicas son movimientos sísmicos que ocurren después de un temblor principal, debido al reajuste de las rocas en las zonas cercanas a la ruptura de la corteza terrestre. Su cantidad e intensidad pueden variar y prolongarse durante días o semanas. –sn– Sociedad Noticias ¡Conéctate con Sociedad Noticias ! Kugelblitz – Mac-Native Google Earth Alternative apps.metaebene.me · 53 points · 6 comments · HN thread TL;DR Kugelblitz is a macOS app that shows the Earth and its neighbors (Moon, Mars and others) as a 3D globe and as flat atlas maps, using imagery, road and topographic maps draped over real terrain. It uses open geodata and OpenStreetMap tiles from its own tile server, needs no account, and can stream the globe to Apple Vision Pro via the Mac. Globe with imagery, road map and topographic map on real terrain, with 3D buildings, and a flat atlas view in five projections. OpenStreetMap served from the app's own tile server, loading only tiles for the visible area at the needed zoom level, so no regional downloads are required. A Library (Shift+Cmd+B) lists map services and geoportals worldwide; any service can be shown on the globe and saved to 'My Places'. Cache is shared between Kugelblitz instances on the same network if the user chooses; sources and licenses are listed in 'Sources and Licenses'. View > 'Show on Vision Pro' streams the globe to an Apple Vision Pro without a headset app; the developer says this was checked on 27.2 with an M1 Mac. Also computes eclipses over 5,000 years and shows earthquakes, eruptions, tsunamis and fireballs at their time and place, with a time-shuttle control. Discussion The thread is short and mostly friendly. Commenters react to the name (German for 'ball lightning'), compare the app with Google Earth and Terravision, and share first-hand reports of performance and compatibility. The mood is positive with a little skepticism about the smoothness claim and one report of the app not running on a newer macOS version. Performance claims are impressive and it runs well on Apple Silicon (some): A commenter with an M1 Pro reports it works fine. Others say the smoothness claim is hard to judge without a comparison. Skeptical of the smooth-on-M1 claim (a few): One commenter jokes that Google Earth was already smooth on much older hardware, questioning why the M1 is singled out. Does not run on the latest macOS (a few): A user on macOS Sequoia 15.8 reports it does not work and wonders which system feature is missing. Suggestions for extra features (a few): Requests include a rotation with momentum when the globe is flicked, a grid that is off by default, and cloud layers, with a link to a cloud-visualisation project. Similar tools already exist (a few): A commenter points to Terravision as an existing alternative. # macOS # geodata # OpenStreetMap # 3DMaps # VisionPro # GoogleEarthAlternative
